name: mia-rosie-midnight-mysteries
description: Mia & Rosie: Midnight Mysteries — English, family-friendly animated supernatural mystery Shorts for ages 6-10: 3D animated, warm female narrator, gentle scares, clever endings.
voice: A warm, expressive female storyteller who sounds like she is sharing a secret at bedtime: suspenseful and friendly, never excessively frightening.
style_rules: Fiction for children aged 6 to 10 and family viewing. Mystery and curiosity first, gentle scares only: no gore, no violence, no cruelty, nothing a child could not watch with a grown-up.
Each episode has a strange event that opens a question, a mystery Mia tries to solve, Rosie behaving a little suspiciously, an age-appropriate reveal, and a memorable last image or line.
Rosie is mysterious, lovable and unpredictable, never purely evil. Mia is curious, brave and sometimes easily frightened.

Write for the ear: short sentences, concrete nouns, strong verbs. No repeated words inside a clip or across clips (the lint enforces this); use 'she', 'the doll' or 'the girl' instead of repeating a name.
Never write the narration as dialogue spoken by an on-screen mouth. Any whisper is narrated as heard from off-screen.
visual_rules: Expressive cinematic 3D animation, midnight blue, lavender and crimson palette, gentle moonlit mystery mood; nothing gory, grimy or realistic-horror.
Recurring characters and the bedroom get locked descriptors in Look anchors, pasted verbatim into every visual prompt where they appear, so faces, clothes and set never drift.
The narrator is off-screen. No character opens its mouth: Mia's lips stay closed and Rosie's stitched mouth never moves.
No text, subtitles, readable words, watermark or logos.
End every visual prompt with: no subtitles, no on-screen text, no watermark, no logos, nobody speaking.
idea_wells: Haunted toys, music boxes and dolls with a clue instead of a jump scare
Bedroom mysteries: footsteps, shadows, mirrors, closets
Original folklore-style enchanted forests and magical objects
